content: I'm refactoring docs#Set to break the defeq with X → Prop. Should docs#Class become a Set or _ → Prop? The file uses one or another in different theorems/definitions.
CC: @Mario Carneiro
Also, should we rename it or move it to a namespace?

We currently define it as Set ZFSet so we get the instances for free, but then we write it out as ZFSet -> Prop to match mathematical notation and avoid mixing up the two membership operations. I think this design was me four year ago's idea.

My current if controversial idea would be to get rid of Class altogether and just write down Set ZFSet directly. Or like, at least make it an abbrev.
That still leaves the question of defeq abuse though...
The former, is my answer to the original question.
I agree that motivates the abuse, but doesn't suggest what way to avoid it
That should be an easy fix, write x \in C instead of C x.
This type is barely used so I imagine that refactor shouldn't take long
I can probably do it if you're willing to give me a day or two
Currently, we have Membership Class Class, not Membership ZFSet Class.
We should have both, I think.
We can't, the first argument is an outParam.
Hm. I guess that would explain why we've been writing C x.
So I guess the correct solution is to define Class := ZFSet → Prop and transfer the relevant instances on Set ZFSet manually.

Yury G. Kudryashov said:

outParam

I don't really understand outParam yet. Why does this prevent you from having the Membership ZFSet Class instance?
Because there is a Membership ZFSet ZFSet instance, obviously.

No, the first argument of Membership is an outParam. So the first argument is always determined purely based on the other argument. So, we can't have both Membership Class Class and Membership ZFSet Class, because it breaks the algorithm that determines the first argument of Membership.

I know that having a Membership Class Class instance is probably inspired by Metamath's approach to classes and has its own advantages, but it's really not what someone familiar with set theory is going to expect.
I saw that in my own set theory course, so I think it's at least somewhat standard? But yeah, maybe we shouldn't have this, for the same reason we don't have things like a Membership Int Nat class.

Violeta Hernández said:

I saw that in my own set theory course, so I think it's at least somewhat standard? But yeah, maybe we shouldn't have this, for the same reason we don't have things like a Membership Int Nat class.

I have never seen it anywhere other than Metamath and Mathlib. What textbook were you using?
I think it's standard in NBG?
Most presentations I've seen of NBG are two-sorted theories.
yeah and you're looking at one here
I'm saying that it's not standard to have a class-in-class membership relation in two-sorted presentations of set theory.
That's the usual way to define membership for classes in NBG that's what I'm saying
I don't really understand your point here though, why do you care about this notation?
Because if you tell a set theorist 'oh by the way, you can't write x∈Cx \in Cx∈C where xxx is a set and CCC is a class', they won't be very happy about it.
but you can?
you can literally write that and it does what you expect
No you can't. There is no Membership ZFSet Class instance.
that's the whole reason for this setup
there is a coercion from ZFSet to Class
so you can write that membership
Ah okay, that was not clear from the previous discussion.

Violeta Hernández said:

Hm. I guess that would explain why we've been writing C x.

It seems like it's not being used in the library though?
the downside is that x \in C is not defeq to C x even though it is provably equal
We definitely write C x before we set up the instances. We can move the instances much earlier so that we use the membership notation everywhere.
I don't remember if we continue using C x after we have the instance.
iirc we had a simp lemma x \in C iff C x

Once people who care about this file agree on what should be there, I can do the refactor (I want to have it done one way or another for the Set refactor, but I don't care which way we fix the defeq abuse).
because of the aforementioned defeq failure, it is useful to have both notations available. What about having a CoeFun instance so that C x works even if you structure wrap everything?
I can do that.
While I have your attention, could you please have a look at #mathlib4 > toNat too?
